summary: Develop practical GIS skills for disease surveillance, health mapping, and programme monitoring. Build maps, assessments, and action plans. Enquire today.
lede: GIS for disease surveillance helps health teams turn case, facility and population data into maps that support programme decisions. For epidemiologists, surveillance staff, programme managers and monitoring specialists, it provides a practical workflow for preparing location data and assessing disease patterns and service coverage. Learners practise data-quality checks, hotspot interpretation and facility-access mapping, then present findings with attention to uncertainty and privacy.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who use health, population, facility, or programme data to monitor disease patterns and guide service delivery. It suits intermediate practitioners who can work with basic spreadsheets or routine health information and need a structured spatial analysis workflow.
prerequisites: You need basic experience working with health programme data, surveillance indicators, or monitoring reports. You do not need prior GIS certification or coding experience. A laptop with QGIS installed is recommended for the practical exercises. Participants using ArcGIS Pro or DHIS2 can relate the workflows to their existing environments, although the guided labs use QGIS and supplied datasets. Advanced spatial statistics, AI-assisted geocoding, and dashboard integration receive operational application or conceptual awareness treatment.
